findings.frozenSummary: Default `all` dashboard period compares against itself, fabricating 0% trends and duplicating the full-history aggregate
findings.impact: The dashboard no longer presents an invented all-time comparison, so managers see unavailable trend data instead of a misleading zero-percent change.

closure.expected: The all-time period has no comparison window and its KPI trends remain null.

findings.note: Current application code passes an optional comparison period, and the focused regression requires null trends for the all-time view.

findings.frozenSummary: Activity paging can throw when it encounters organization resource rows because the allowed-resource vocabulary is incomplete
findings.impact: Activity paging now uses the shared complete resource vocabulary, so organization entries do not interrupt the manager's activity view.

closure.expected: Repository row mapping validates against the shared resource catalogue that includes organization activity.

findings.note: The repository-local incomplete list was removed and the shared activity vocabulary includes created organization rows.

findings.frozenSummary: `deescalated` is missing from the constructor allowlist, silently dropping escalation-resolved audit rows
findings.impact: Resolved escalations remain visible in activity history, preserving a consistent managerial audit trail.

closure.expected: Escalation-resolved events map to deescalated inbox-item activity.

findings.note: The shared vocabulary contains deescalated and the focused event-handler regression asserts the mapped action and resource type.

findings.frozenSummary: Invitation acceptance errors skip tagged mapping and surface as 500s
findings.impact: Invitation problems now produce the intended user-facing response instead of an unexplained server error.

closure.expected: A tagged invitation-not-found result is mapped to the expected 404 response.

findings.note: The acceptance handler now performs the same tagged error mapping as the surrounding invitation actions, with focused regression coverage.

findings.frozenSummary: One Query key is shared by incompatible invitation response shapes
findings.impact: User invitations and organization invitations no longer overwrite each other's cached response shape, keeping both screens consistent.

closure.expected: Each incompatible invitation response shape owns a distinct child query key and each route uses the corresponding key.

findings.note: The current key hierarchy retains a shared invalidation prefix while separating user and organization invitation data.

findings.frozenSummary: Recognition settings use loader-held/mirrored state and invalidate a key no query owns; mutations can leave stale UI

closure.expected: Before recognition is activated, replace initial-prop mirrors with one authoritative Query/Form flow and align mutation invalidation with an owned query key.

findings.note: The current route redirects to the unavailable page, but the retained component is byte-identical to the frozen initial-state implementation.

findings.frozenSummary: Reply UI mirrors Query data and can remain “Publishing…” after the cache updates; must be rechecked after the active inbox merge
findings.impact: Reply publication status now follows refreshed server data without remounting, so managers do not remain stuck on a stale Publishing state.

closure.expected: The editor renders the authoritative reply prop and leaves Publishing when a server refresh reports publication.

findings.note: The mirror was removed, and the interaction story exercises a server refresh from publishing to published without remounting the editor.

findings.frozenSummary: Manager property rows are clickable non-interactive `div`s, blocking keyboard access to primary navigation
findings.impact: The primary property navigation is now a focus-visible link, making the property list usable with a keyboard and consistent with browser navigation semantics.

findings.note: The clickable row div was replaced by a TanStack Link and the story asserts its link role and href.

findings.frozenSummary: Staff responsibility edits can be reset by effect resynchronization after parent/query changes; the old “fresh array every render” explanation was too broad

closure.expected: The open modal does not resynchronize local edits on a parent refresh and submits against the expected revision.

findings.note: The resynchronizing effect is absent, the update carries an expected revision, and the focused story preserves a checked portal across a simulated query refresh.

findings.frozenSummary: Organization rename/update does not invalidate active-organization data, leaving stale navigation/header state
findings.impact: Organization changes now refresh the active organization cache, keeping navigation and header labels aligned with saved settings.

closure.expected: A successful organization update invalidates the active-organization query key.

findings.note: The route delegates successful updates to a named cache policy and its focused test fixes the exact invalidation contract.

findings.frozenSummary: Inbox detail/status/autosave paths use overly broad invalidation, causing list/count refetch storms; must be rechecked after the active inbox merge
findings.impact: Reply draft and state changes now patch only the selected detail, status commands invalidate only folder-owned data, and the status observer is selected-item scoped, preventing the former broad request recurrence.

closure.expected: Draft autosave causes no additional detail, notes, activity, list, count, or last-visit request; A-to-B-to-A selection requests each item's detail and notes once per transition; status observation never crosses item identities.

findings.note: Typed reply-change classification patches only the selected detail. Folder caches change only for status transitions, the observer is item-identity scoped, and real QueryObserver regressions pin request counts for selection changes and autosave. Hosted browser proof remains package-level evidence, not a condition for closing this code finding.

findings.frozenSummary: Inbox last-visit badge has no production stamp call, so “since last visit” becomes total open count

closure.expected: The production inbox page stamps one successful visit per organization and refreshes the dependent badge query.

findings.note: The page waits for a successful load, records once per organization, and delegates badge refresh to the inbox cache policy.

findings.frozenSummary: Import detail route omits the role gate used by its index route; server authorization still protects effects
